First time at a Fukuoka yatai? Most stalls seat no more than about 10 people, and the city's own tourism site lists a few house rules. Three things first-timers get wrong, and the easy fix 👇

👀 One of these surprised even us 👉 https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-where-to-stay-first-trip

❌ MISTAKE 1: ARRIVING WITH YOUR SUITCASE

Yatai have nowhere to put luggage. Drop it at the hotel or a coin locker first, which is easy when your hotel is 5 minutes from the airport.

❌ MISTAKE 2: SITTING WITHOUT ORDERING

One order per person is the basic rule. Fast turnover keeps a stall alive, so eat, pay and try a second stall instead of staying for hours.

❌ MISTAKE 3: COMING AS A BIG GROUP

Two or three people slip in easily. Six people means waiting, or splitting up.

✅ THE FIX

Go in a small group from about 6 pm, start at the river stalls in Nakasu, then hop. Nagahama, by the fish market, came back to life in 2023; Nagahama no Hiroshi starts many evenings with a ¥900 pork-wrapped lettuce roll.

🌧️ One honest warning: on stormy nights some stalls simply don't open. If yatai are the reason for your trip, give yourself two evenings.

Sharing one small counter with strangers and the owner, under a canvas roof by the river: that's the part of Fukuoka people remember.
